original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Construct a bounded iterative compact prefix-key index, prove O(LG) key preparation instead of cold quadratic prefix materialization, and test complete current native runtime without dropping checks.
scope_change_reason: The measured runtime target did not pass. The delivered scope is the exact key-work construction and a recorded negative complete-component experiment, rather than a claimed runtime speedup.
bottleneck_link: Explicit negative evidence prevents pursuing compact key preparation as a demonstrated speedup of the current native replay; the reusable key bound is separate from native and compiler admission.
stop_rule: Stop after the first bounded compact-key construction and five complete alternating pairs; if no speedup appears, retain the failed method and report the narrower result.
evidence: PROOF.md proves exact state preservation and the key-work bound. verify.py checks source/fork preservation, exact states, cache invalidation and the complete native receipt. Both five-pair experiments are retained.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can one actual native component profit from the compact key bound after all preparation is charged?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current complete-component measurements do not demonstrate a runtime gain.
open_questions.first_step: Identify a different measured prefix-length and miss-rate regime before another implementation change.
open_questions.blocked_by: No measured current-native speedup; extra interner and route memory must be priced.

open_questions.question: Can the current native replay be improved by changing a larger measured cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Key preparation is only part of the complete component.
open_questions.first_step: Profile the unchanged algebra/tableau or gate-table work and propose one changed algorithm with the same receipt.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such change is constructed or reserved here.
